report.headline: Strong celebrity-driven open; board-room wide shots and a long product card are the two opportunities
report.summary: The ad sits well above typical for most of its runtime, with seeing and hearing both leading engagement while understanding stays reliably above typical from start through the mid-section. The comedic premise lands clearly. The main weaknesses are a mid-video dip when the board-room scene holds a wide, face-free composition, and a closing product card that pushes seeing and overall below typical.

moments.what_happens: Michael Cera holds the CeraVe jar up toward the camera and glances at it with a smirk.
moments.brain_response: Seeing and hearing are both well above typical as the product reveal and deadpan reaction land together.

moments.what_happens: Two faces appear at the massage table, then the edit cuts to a climber pressed against a sheer cliff face.
moments.brain_response: Seeing reaches the video's highest point, well above typical, driven by the strong visual contrast and close faces.

moments.what_happens: A wide board-room shot holds for several seconds with the footage playing small on a screen at the far end.
moments.brain_response: Hearing drops to near and then just below typical, and overall falls to its weakest mid-video level, though understanding stays above typical.
moments.suggestion: Cut to a tighter shot of one or two audience members reacting to the footage to recover visual and hearing engagement.

moments.what_happens: Three professionals appear in close-up with the CeraVe logo behind them, then cut to Michael Cera smiling and raising a finger.
moments.brain_response: Understanding peaks and overall recovers as faces and brand framing return.

moments.what_happens: A static product shot holds with on-screen text reading 'Developed with Dermatologists. Not Michael Cera.'
moments.brain_response: Seeing falls below typical and overall drops below typical for the first time in the video, with the last second the lowest point of the ad.
moments.suggestion: Trim the card to two seconds or keep Michael Cera visible in the frame alongside the product to prevent the response falling off at the close.

strengths: The celebrity face speaking directly to camera builds both seeing and hearing well above typical within the first few seconds, giving the ad a confident start.
Understanding stays above typical from the opening through the mid-section, showing the comedic premise reads clearly without needing the sound.
improvements: The board-room sequence uses a prolonged wide composition that loses the close faces driving engagement earlier in the ad.
The final product card is long enough that seeing and overall slip below typical, weakening the last impression the ad leaves.

report.headline: Witty celebrity campaign runs well above typical — dark opening and CGI narwhal are the two moments to tighten
report.summary: The video is above typical for most of its run, with seeing, hearing and understanding all contributing positively. Hearing reaches the single highest point in the video the moment Michael Cera's face appears and he begins speaking, and the combination of face, product and declared identity drives the overall peak around seconds 18 to 22. Understanding is the weakest group across the video and dips below typical in the narwhal sequence. The clearest opportunity is the opening, which spends several seconds on empty dark curtains before any face appears and starts well below typical.

moments.what_happens: Dark curtains fill the frame with only a brief, shadowy silhouette — no face, no product.
moments.brain_response: All three groups start below typical, making this a genuinely weak opening rather than a normal build.
moments.suggestion: Cut to Michael Cera's face or the product reveal sooner to avoid starting below typical.

moments.what_happens: Michael Cera's face is revealed in close-up and he introduces himself as he holds up the product.
moments.brain_response: Hearing surges to the highest single-second value in the entire video, lifting overall well above typical.

moments.what_happens: He reaches through a curtain holding the cream, a 'GENEROSITY' title appears on screen, and he declares 'I am CeraVe.'
moments.brain_response: Hearing, understanding and seeing are all elevated together, reaching the video's overall peak.

moments.what_happens: A CGI narwhal rises from the water in a lush illustrated environment, with on-screen subtitles praising Michael Cera's skin.
moments.brain_response: Understanding dips below typical, hearing falls near or below typical, and overall drops to just above zero — the weakest non-ending stretch in the video.
moments.suggestion: A brief cut back to Michael Cera reacting to the narwhal would anchor understanding and keep it above typical.

moments.what_happens: The curtains clear and the brand logo card holds on a white background.
moments.brain_response: Overall falls below typical, as expected for a short end card.

strengths: Seeing stays above typical for almost the entire video, sustained by consistent close-ups of Michael Cera's face alongside the product.
The speech-driven identity reveal — 'I am CeraVe' — lifts hearing and understanding simultaneously, creating the video's strongest stretch.
improvements: The opening runs several seconds of dark curtains before a face appears, starting all groups below typical; moving the face reveal earlier would turn this into a genuine strength.
Understanding is the weakest group throughout and slips below typical in the narwhal sequence; grounding that scene with a faster return to a human face would close the gap.

samples.title: Sintel (trailer)
samples.attribution: © copyright Blender Foundation | durian.blender.org, CC BY 3.0

report.headline: Seeing and hearing lead this trailer well above typical; a dark open and long title card are the main opportunities.
report.summary: Overall this trailer sits above typical for most of its running time, with seeing and hearing as the two leading groups while understanding plays a supporting role. The sustained peak runs from the combat sequence through the ruined castle panorama, roughly seconds 17 to 27, where both seeing and hearing are well above typical. A dark opening and a lengthy title card at each end pull the response below typical and offer the clearest opportunities for improvement.

moments.what_happens: The video opens on a completely black frame before any image appears.
moments.brain_response: Overall is below typical from the first frame, with seeing and understanding both notably below typical.
moments.suggestion: Opening directly on the snowy landscape or the masked character would bring the response to typical more quickly.

moments.what_happens: A title card gives way to a tight close-up of an elder character who speaks.
moments.brain_response: Hearing reaches the video's highest point, lifting overall well above typical.

moments.what_happens: A fight in the snow cuts through ruins to a wide sunset panorama of a crumbling castle with flying creatures.
moments.brain_response: Both seeing and hearing are well above typical throughout, making this the video's strongest sustained stretch overall.

moments.what_happens: A creature's stinger attacks the woman, then aerial shots show her being carried away.
moments.brain_response: Seeing reaches the video's absolute highest, but hearing falls below typical, pulling overall sharply downward toward near-typical.
moments.suggestion: Holding on the woman's face for a moment before cutting to the wider aerial grab shots could slow the overall decline.

moments.what_happens: The title appears on a black background, followed by a credits screen.
moments.brain_response: Overall falls well below typical and continues declining through the end of the credits.
moments.suggestion: Trimming the title and credits sequence to around five seconds would limit this prolonged drop.

strengths: The close-up of the elder at second 12, paired with spoken dialogue, delivers the video's peak hearing response alongside rising understanding, giving that moment the best-rounded engagement of the trailer.
Seeing stays well above typical from the first character shot at second 6 through the entire creature sequence, providing a strong and consistent visual backbone.
improvements: The black opening holds overall below typical for the first two seconds; starting immediately on an active shot would reach typical sooner.

The wide desert shots from second 36 onward drop seeing toward and below typical and ease overall to near typical; a brief cut to the woman's face before the title appears would add a lift into the title reveal.

samples.title: Big Buck Bunny (55 s excerpt)
samples.attribution: © copyright 2008, Blender Foundation | www.bigbuckbunny.org, CC BY 3.0

report.headline: Seeing carries this animated short well above typical; a mid-film meadow dip is the main opportunity
report.summary: Seeing leads throughout the entire video, never falling below typical, and drives two strong peaks. Hearing adds lift during the close-up face sequences and especially in the final stretch, while understanding stays near or below typical for almost the whole film. A clear dip in the middle — where the rabbit stands alone inspecting an apple in a wide meadow — pulls overall well below typical. The video recovers strongly, finishing at its highest overall point as the butterfly returns in the final seconds.

moments.what_happens: The rabbit appears at a mossy burrow and is then shown in low-angle shots against the sky before a close-up of its face at second 5.
moments.brain_response: Overall stays near typical throughout the opening, with seeing only gently above and hearing just below — a slower build than the close-up sequences later deliver.
moments.suggestion: Opening on the expressive close-up face rather than the wide burrow and upward-looking shots would give seeing a stronger lift from the first frame.

moments.what_happens: The rabbit moves into a field of oversized daisies, sniffs them in close-up, then lies in the grass as a pink butterfly lands on it.
moments.brain_response: Overall climbs steadily to one of the video's two peak levels, with seeing rising strongly and hearing also above typical once the butterfly appears.

moments.what_happens: The rabbit stands in an open meadow examining a small red apple, shown in wide shots with little change in framing.
moments.brain_response: This is the video's clearest dip, with overall well below typical; hearing drops to its lowest point of the entire film and pulls overall further down than the pictures alone would.
moments.suggestion: Tighter shots of the rabbit's face while it scrutinises the apple would keep seeing stronger and reduce how far the overall level falls.

moments.what_happens: The camera closes in on the rabbit's brooding face as a purple butterfly lands first on its ear, then its face, and the rabbit stares it down.
moments.brain_response: All three groups rise together to the video's highest sustained overall level, with hearing reaching its peak for the entire film in the final seconds.

strengths: Seeing stays above typical for the entire video, sustained by the character's expressive animated face and richly detailed environments.
The final stretch brings all three groups above typical together and hearing to its highest level of the film, making the last seconds the video's strongest.
improvements: Hearing falls well below typical across the apple-inspection stretch and makes it the drag that tips overall below 0 even when seeing remains near neutral — that scene is the primary opportunity in the film.

The two scenes where the squirrel watches the rabbit are framed overhead and at a distance, limiting how much social context the viewer can read; a closer shot of both characters together would give understanding more to engage with.

report.headline: B draws stronger brain engagement overall, but A opens better and holds up where B fades to its title card
report.summary: These are two entirely different animated films — A is the comedic Big Buck Bunny, B is the dramatic Sintel — not two cuts of the same video. B is predicted above A in hearing and understanding across most of the shared running time, lifted by its dialogue exchanges and action sequences, making it stronger in well over half the shared seconds. A wins the opening clearly and pulls ahead again in the final stretch, where B has given way to a lengthy title card and credits.

differences.what_differs: A opens on a bright sunlit meadow with the rabbit already in frame; B opens on a black screen fading into dark grey snowscapes with no characters visible.
differences.brain_response: A's seeing starts above typical immediately; B's seeing and understanding start clearly below typical and take several seconds to recover, a weaker opening.

differences.what_differs: B cuts to close-up faces of characters delivering dialogue ('What brings you to the land of the gatekeepers?' / 'I'm searching for someone'); A shows the rabbit wordlessly sniffing flowers in a wide garden shot.
differences.brain_response: B's hearing surges far above typical — its highest peak in the video — while understanding also rises clearly above typical; A's hearing stays near or just above 0 and understanding stays slightly below, leaving B well ahead on both groups throughout this stretch.

differences.what_differs: A continues with lively character animation — the rabbit inspecting an apple, then interacting with a butterfly on his face; B transitions to a wide desert shot with a title card, then to several seconds of a logo on black, then to a credits screen.
differences.brain_response: A's seeing and hearing climb steadily above typical; B's seeing, hearing and understanding all fall well below typical during the logo and credits, creating the largest gap between the two videos in any stretch.

a_does_better: A's opening is above typical from the very first shot, while B's dark, empty start holds all groups below typical for the first few seconds.
A sustains above-typical seeing and hearing through its final character scenes, whereas B's late title card and credits pull all groups clearly below typical.
b_does_better: B's dialogue scenes drive hearing far above typical — its strongest group throughout the film — while A's near-wordless story keeps hearing near or below typical for most of its run.
B's action sequences and dramatic character close-ups across the mid-section lift seeing and understanding well above typical, giving B its lead across the majority of shared seconds.
suggestions: B's first four seconds — a black screen and near-black snowscape — start all groups below typical; opening on the first recognisable character shot sooner would give the hearing and seeing curves a faster lift.

B's logo screen runs for roughly five seconds on a plain black background before the credits appear; trimming it to two or three seconds would reduce the depth and duration of the late-video drop without losing the title.

report.headline: A and B are nearly matched overall; A opens stronger, B peaks slightly higher mid-video
report.summary: These are two cuts of the same CeraVe campaign, with B running roughly 45 seconds longer than A. Across their shared material the overall response is almost identical—neither is ahead in clearly more seconds—but A's immediate on-camera opening holds hearing and understanding well above typical from the first second, while B's curtain-and-silhouette introduction keeps the response below typical for the first eight seconds. B recovers and edges ahead from around 17 seconds onward, reaching a slightly higher combined peak during its close-up product and character section, though its abstract curtain and fantasy-garden passage is its weakest sustained stretch.

differences.what_differs: A opens immediately on Michael Cera speaking directly to camera and holding up the product; B opens on empty dark curtains and an obscured silhouette with no speech.
differences.brain_response: A is well above typical from the very first second, with hearing and understanding both strongly positive; B keeps all three groups below typical for the first eight seconds, with understanding particularly suppressed.

differences.what_differs: A cuts to a wide boardroom shot as an establishing scene; B stays on close-up character and product footage accompanied by on-screen titles and speech.
differences.brain_response: B's hearing and understanding rise together to reach their joint peak for the video, pushing overall well above typical; A's hearing drops to near and then below typical as the wide boardroom shot displaces the character close-up, leaving B clearly ahead throughout this stretch.

differences.what_differs: B moves through abstract curtain wipes with a text overlay followed by an animated narwhal sequence—content with no equivalent in A.
differences.brain_response: Hearing and understanding both fall below typical and seeing softens, pulling B's overall response to its lowest sustained level in the video.

a_does_better: A drives hearing and understanding above typical from the very first second, with no warm-up lag
A avoids any extended below-typical stretch, staying above typical for nearly its entire duration
b_does_better: B's mid-video close-up product and character section brings hearing and understanding to a higher combined peak than anything A reaches
The extended rock-climbing sequence keeps seeing well above typical for longer than A's shorter version of the same material
suggestions: Cut or substantially shorten B's dark curtain introduction and open sooner on the character speaking to camera, as A does, to avoid the eight-second below-typical drag at the start
Tighten or replace the abstract curtain-wipe and narwhal passage in B with a closer character or product moment to prevent the sustained dip in hearing and understanding mid-video
